name: Feedback loops
originator: Norbert Wiener (cybernetics); Jay Forrester; Donella Meadows
rule: Reinforcing loops snowball, balancing loops stabilise, and delays cause overshoot and oscillation.
plain: Outputs feed back into inputs. Find the loops and you understand why the system behaves the way it does.

story.beat: Ada wires CO2 injection to boost plant growth. The sensor reads with a 6-hour delay. CO2 is low, so she injects; the reading doesn't change yet, so she injects more. Six hours later CO2 overshoots and the plants suffer. She cuts it, and it undershoots. The delay turned a balancing loop into a wobble. Meanwhile sick plants make less oxygen, stressing the healthy ones, which then get sick: a reinforcing loop.

examples.text: Rumour of a water shortage → hoarding → real shortage → more hoarding. A reinforcing loop, like a bank run.
Thermostats form a balancing loop: too cold → heat on → warm → heat off.
Order delays make supply managers over-order, then under-order: the bullwhip effect.

realCase.title: The Beer Game
realCase.text: In MIT's supply-chain simulation, players manage one link of a beer supply chain with delayed orders. Almost every team produces wild swings of shortage and glut from one small change in customer demand. They blame each other, but the cause is the delay in the loop.
realCase.source: John Sterman, 'Modeling Managerial Behavior', Management Science 35 (1989)

misuse: Drawing loops for everything until the diagram explains nothing. A loop map is a hypothesis; check it against data.

videos.title: LOOPY: a tool for thinking in systems (interactive)

animation.note: One of the 2 code-made animations: a delayed balancing loop overshooting and oscillating, compared with the same loop without delay.

predict.prompt: The CO2 sensor has a 6-hour delay. Ada adjusts injection every hour based on it. What happens?
options: CO2 overshoots and swings back and forth
predict.why: Acting on delayed information in a balancing loop causes oscillation.

mcq.why: Each withdrawal makes the next more likely.

whichModel.prompt: A shower goes from freezing to scalding because the water takes a few seconds to reach you.
whichModel.why: A balancing loop with a delay.
